description: Converted Airship Engineer paths and gadget schematics.

entries.title: Ship Engineer Path
entries.summary: Ship Engineers specialize in hull integrity, field repair, engine overdrive, and coordinated damage control.
body: This is a converted specialization for [[airship-engineer-class|Airship Engineer]]. Choose it when the parent class grants its path or domain at 3rd level.

sections.heading: Converted path progression
body: Path feature I — Hull Fortification (3rd): After 10 minutes of work, grant one vessel or vehicle temporary hit points equal to 5 × engineer level. Only one vessel may benefit at a time. Quick Repairs also allows Rapid Repair to affect a ship zone from 10 feet away when connected by tools, lines, or a repair drone.

Path feature II — Engine Overdrive (7th): Spend 2 ingenuity points as a standard action. For 5 rounds the vessel gains +25 percent speed and +2 on control checks. When the effect ends, the engine must succeed on a DC 15 maintenance check or become fatigued, taking -2 on control checks for 10 minutes.

Path feature III — Repair Crew (11th): Allies using aid another on your repair checks grant +4 instead of +2. Once per encounter, a successful Rapid Repair also restores half that amount to a second adjacent ship component.
Path feature IV — Structural Reinforcement (15th): Spend 3 ingenuity points to grant one ship zone damage reduction 5/— for 10 rounds. At 19th engineer level this becomes damage reduction 10/—.

Path feature V — Master of Engines (19th): Engine Overdrive no longer risks engine fatigue, its control bonus becomes +4, and once per day Shipwright's Touch repairs 10d6 + Intelligence modifier hit points divided among connected vessel components.

sections.heading: Use with the base class
body: The five features are gained at parent-class levels 3, 7, 11, 15, and 19 respectively.
Unless a feature states otherwise, save DC equals 10 + one-half parent-class level + the parent class’s key ability modifier.
This path does not replace the parent class’s base attack, saves, skills, resource pool, bonus feats, or core class features.

sourceRefs.notes: Converted five-stage specialization for the twenty-level parent class.

entries.title: Sky Machine Engineer Path
entries.summary: Sky Machine Engineers turn temporary devices into battlefield weapons, defenders, and protective machines.
body: This is a converted specialization for [[airship-engineer-class|Airship Engineer]]. Choose it when the parent class grants its path or domain at 3rd level.

sections.heading: Converted path progression
body: Path feature I — Deployable Turret (3rd): Spend 1 ingenuity point and a standard action to deploy a Tiny turret in an adjacent square for 5 rounds. It has AC 15 + one-half engineer level, hit points equal to 5 + twice engineer level, and makes one ranged attack each round using engineer base attack + Intelligence modifier for 1d8 piercing, fire, cold, or electricity damage.

Path feature II — Enhanced Weaponry (7th): Spend 1 point during 10 minutes of work to add 1d6 fire, cold, electricity, or sonic damage to one weapon or ship weapon on its first successful hit each round for 1 hour.

Path feature III — Automated Defenders (11th): Spend 3 points to deploy three defender drones for 10 rounds. Each drone may intercept one attack against an adjacent ally, granting +2 shield AC; a drone is destroyed after intercepting two attacks.
Path feature IV — Mechanical Shielding (15th): Spend 2 points as an immediate action to grant a creature, construct, or ship zone temporary hit points equal to 5 + twice engineer level for 5 rounds.

Path feature V — Overclocking (19th): Spend 3 points to double the range, area, movement bonus, repair dice, or damage dice of one engineer gadget for 5 rounds. The gadget becomes disabled afterward until repaired during 1 hour of work.

entries.title: Tinker Engineer Path
entries.summary: Tinker Engineers specialize in traps, rapid fabrication, utility devices, and independent creations.
body: This is a converted specialization for [[airship-engineer-class|Airship Engineer]]. Choose it when the parent class grants its path or domain at 3rd level.

sections.heading: Converted path progression
body: Path feature I — Trapmaking (3rd): In 5 minutes and for 10 gp per engineer level, create a mechanical trap occupying one square. Search and Disable Device DC equal 10 + one-half engineer level + Intelligence modifier. When triggered it deals 1d6 damage per three engineer levels, maximum 6d6, with a Reflex save for half. Choose bludgeoning, piercing, fire, acid, or electricity when built.

Path feature II — Quick Construction (7th): Temporary gadgets, traps, and invention-system prototypes require half the normal work units and time, minimum 10 minutes. Once per encounter spend 1 ingenuity point to assemble one known simple gadget as a full-round action.

Path feature III — Trap Mastery (11th): A trap may replace 2d6 damage with one effect: blinded for 1 round, entangled for 1d4 rounds, knocked prone, or pushed 10 feet. A successful save negates the added effect.

Path feature IV — Clockwork Companion (15th): Build one Small construct companion using 500 gp in parts and 3 days of work. It has Hit Dice equal to one-half engineer level, base attack equal to engineer level, AC 18, Strength 14, Dexterity 16, and follows simple commands. Rebuilding a destroyed companion costs half the original materials.

Path feature V — Master Tinker (19th): Maintain one master creation such as an improved companion, one-person floating platform, portable workshop, or master trap. Treat it as an advanced invention with one free improvement and no minor flaw.

entries.title: Airship Engineer Gadget Schematics
entries.summary: Temporary schematic gadgets used by the converted Airship Engineer and available as permanent inventions through the crafting system.
body: An Airship Engineer records schematics rather than preparing spells. Temporary gadgets are assembled through the class’s Schematic Book and powered with ingenuity points.
A permanent, commercial, or ship-integrated version must be constructed through [[invention-system|the invention system]] and may require a larger installation, power source, crew, or certification.

sections.heading: Core schematics
body: Emergency Grappling Winch: 1 point; swift action; one creature gains a 20-foot climb speed and +4 on Climb and Use Rope for 5 rounds, or launches a hook 60 feet as a ranged touch attack. A resisting target makes Reflex against the engineer’s class DC or becomes tethered.
Repair Drone: 1 point; standard action; flies 30 feet and restores 1d6 + one-half engineer level hit points to an object, construct, or ship component. It cannot restore destroyed parts.
Smoke Dispersal Unit: 1 point; standard action; creates a 10-foot-radius smoke cloud within 30 feet for 5 rounds. Wind disperses it normally.
Static Discharge Array: 1 point; standard action; 30-foot line dealing 1d6 electricity per two engineer levels, maximum 10d6; Reflex half.
Kinetic Stabilizer: 1 point; immediate action; halve falling, collision, or forced-movement damage to one creature, object, or vehicle zone within 30 feet.
Flame Vent: 1 point; standard action; 15-foot cone dealing 1d6 fire per two engineer levels, maximum 10d6; Reflex half.

sections.heading: Advanced schematics
body: Reinforced Plating: 1 point; standard action; grants +2 armor AC or +2 natural armor to one creature, object, or vehicle zone for 5 rounds.
Burst Booster: 1 point; swift action; grants +20 feet personal speed or +25 percent vessel speed for 1 round.
Arcane Dampener: 2 points; standard action; grants +2 resistance on saves against spells and spell-like abilities for 5 rounds, or +2 on a vessel system’s checks against magical disruption.
Sonic Pulse Generator: 2 points; standard action; creatures in a 15-foot cone take 1d6 sonic damage per three levels, maximum 6d6, and pass Fortitude or be pushed 10 feet.
Thermal Shielding: 2 points; standard action; grants fire and cold resistance 10 for 10 minutes per class level. At 14th level resistance becomes 20.
Auto-Repair Module: 3 points; full-round installation; restores 1 hit point per engineer level each round for 5 rounds to one object, construct, or vehicle zone, ending if the target is destroyed.

sections.heading: Gadget rules
body: Temporary gadgets require appropriate tools and ordinary parts included in class upkeep. A gadget is not a spell, does not provoke spell resistance, and is normally extraordinary unless its description is explicitly magical.
A creature can identify and disable an unattended gadget with Search and Disable Device against the engineer’s class DC. Destroying a gadget ends its effect.
Numerical damage and repair values are character-scale. Ship-scale rules may convert them into structural values according to the vessel system in use.

sourceRefs.notes: Converted gadget chart using d20 actions, save DCs, and typed bonuses.
